topStory.headline: UK Company Bundles Free Student A.I. Access With Staff Licenses
topStory.summary:
ICS.AI has launched a model that gives UK university students free access to institutional A.I. tools when universities purchase staff licenses, according to IT Brief UK. The company reports that fewer than 5% of the UK's 2.9 million higher education students currently have access to structured institutional A.I. tools, while 57% of employers report significant A.I. skills gaps.

For an institution with 20,000 students, annual spending on commercial A.I. services can reach millions, making universal access financially prohibitive for many institutions. ICS.AI's CEO Martin Neale describes this access gap as a potential defining driver of graduate employability.

The company emphasizes governance, audit trails, and compliance controls in its platform. The bundled approach positions A.I. literacy as basic educational infrastructure similar to internet access or library resources. The model addresses the cost barrier that has created a divide between students who can afford individual A.I. subscriptions and those who cannot.

stories.headline: NSF Awards $11M for K-12 A.I. Teacher Training
stories.summary: The National Science Foundation awarded $11 million to the Computer Science Teachers Association to train 2,500-3,000 K-12 educators in A.I. and computer science foundations, according to Mirage News. The program will operate across seven states and aims to reach 500,000-600,000 students over two years.

stories.headline: Oxford School Launches A.I. Micro-School for Sixth Form
stories.summary: Wychwood School launched A.I. Futures Oxford, offering an A-level in Artificial Intelligence for students aged 16 and over, according to IT Brief UK. The program operates outside normal school hours, allowing students to stay at their current schools while adding A.I. education.

stories.headline: Dutch Lecturer Calls for Student-Centered A.I. Approach
stories.summary: University of Amsterdam lecturer Nicos Starreveld argues that excessive focus on A.I.-secure testing undermines trust between faculty and students, according to Folia.nl. He advocates for emphasizing student learning and well-being over assessment security, suggesting A.I.-secure assignments should focus on affective learning domains.

stories.headline: Survey: 70% of Students Use A.I. Weekly, 48% Seek Guidance on Social Media
stories.summary: A Jobs for the Future survey found 70% of students use A.I. weekly for education, up from 59% in 2024, according to Inside Higher Ed. However, 48% seek A.I. guidance from social media versus 23% from educational institutions, indicating students prefer informal learning channels despite increased institutional training offerings.

stories.headline: White House Releases A.I. Policy Framework for Congress
stories.summary: The White House released a National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence with legislative recommendations emphasizing innovation over restrictive regulation, according to the Center for Data Innovation. The Center praised the framework for addressing legitimate concerns while avoiding barriers to A.I. deployment and calling for federal preemption of conflicting state laws.
